20261119-chemistry-g07.material: At constant temperature, the pressure of a gas with a volume of 60 mL at 1 atm was raised to 3 atm. According to Boyle's law, what is the volume of this gas?
20261119-chemistry-g07.thinking.1: ការវែកញែកសមហេតុផលនិងការវិភាគ
20261119-chemistry-g07.s.s1.prompt: At constant temperature, the pressure of a gas with a volume of 60 mL at 1 atm was raised to 3 atm. According to Boyle's law, what is the volume of this gas?
20261119-chemistry-g07.s.s1.explain: According to Boyle's law, $P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2$ holds at constant temperature. $1\text{ atm} \times 60\text{ mL} = 3\text{ atm} \times V_2 \implies V_2 = 20\text{ mL}$.

20261121-chemistry-g07-1.s.s1.explain: As altitude increases, atmospheric pressure decreases. The pressure of the gas inside the bag becomes greater than the outside atmospheric pressure, so the volume of the gas inside expands until the inside and outside pressures become equal.
20261121-chemistry-g07-1.s.s1.hint.0: At higher altitude, the air thins and atmospheric pressure decreases.
20261121-chemistry-g07-1.s.s1.hint.1: When the external pressure becomes smaller, the volume of the gas increases (Boyle's law).
20261121-chemistry-g07-1.s.s1.o.o0: Because the higher you go up the mountain, the lower the atmospheric pressure (external pressure) becomes, so the volume of the gas inside the snack bag expanded
20261121-chemistry-g07-1.s.s1.o.o1: Because the temperature on the mountain was too high and the gas expanded

20261121-chemistry-g07-1.s.s1.o.o3: Because oxygen on the mountain seeped into the snack bag

20261122-chemistry-g07-1.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced Diffusion Rate] Cotton soaked in concentrated ammonia water (molecular mass 17) and cotton soaked in concentrated hydrochloric acid (molecular mass 36.5) were placed at the same time at the two ends of a long glass tube and the ends were plugged with rubber stoppers. After a while, a band of white smoke (ammonium chloride) formed inside the glass tube. Where is it located, closer to which end?
20261122-chemistry-g07-1.s.s1.explain: The diffusion rate of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molecular mass. Ammonia gas, which is light with a molecular mass of 17, travels much faster than the heavier hydrogen chloride gas (36.5), so the two gases meet and react at a position closer to the hydrochloric acid cotton, where the relatively slower hydrogen chloride has moved less, forming the white smoke band.
20261122-chemistry-g07-1.s.s1.hint.0: The lighter the gas molecules, the faster they diffuse (Graham's law of diffusion).
20261122-chemistry-g07-1.s.s1.hint.1: Ammonia (17) is much lighter than hydrogen chloride (36.5).

20261122-chemistry-g07-2.s.s1.hint.1: When the temperature gets very low, gas molecules slow down almost to a standstill.
20261122-chemistry-g07-2.s.s1.o.o0: At extremely low temperature the kinetic energy of the gas molecules in the balloon becomes extremely sluggish, so the distance between molecules decreases

20261121-chemistry-g08-2.s.s1.prompt: To check whether chloride ions (Cl⁻), left in tap water as a disinfection by-product, are present, which reagent should be added, and what is the chemical formula of the white precipitate formed?
20261121-chemistry-g08-2.s.s1.explain: When the silver ions ($\text{Ag}^+$) in silver nitrate solution react with the chloride ions ($\text{Cl}^-$) in the water, they form a white silver chloride ($\text{AgCl}$) precipitate that does not dissolve in water, so chloride ions can be detected.
20261121-chemistry-g08-2.s.s1.hint.0: When silver ions (Ag⁺) meet chloride ions (Cl⁻), a white precipitate that does not dissolve in water forms.
20261121-chemistry-g08-2.s.s1.hint.1: Precipitation reaction equation: Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ → AgCl↓

20261122-chemistry-g08-2.s.s1.explain: According to the electrolysis equation of water, $2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g)$, hydrogen gas is produced at the (-) electrode, where reduction occurs, in a volume of $2$, and oxygen gas is produced at the (+) electrode, where oxidation occurs, in a volume of $1$.
